--!nocheck
--[[
	Runtime tests for the Luau half of `@rbxts/svg`.

	These run the *compiled* package — the Luau `rbxtsc` emitted — against IR
	produced by the real Rust compiler. That makes them the test that actually
	proves the two halves of the format agree: `crates/svg-ir` writes the bytes,
	and this reads them back with an entirely separate implementation.

	Run with `pnpm test:luau`, which regenerates the bundle first.
]]

local harness = require("./harness")
local sources = require("./sources")
local fixtures = require("./fixtures")

-- The standalone luau CLI has no Roblox datatypes. Vector2 (sizes) and Color3
-- (currentColor) are the only two the package reaches for.
local Vector2 = {}
Vector2.__index = Vector2
function Vector2.new(x, y)
	return setmetatable({ X = x, Y = y }, Vector2)
end
Vector2.zero = Vector2.new(0, 0)

local Color3 = {}
Color3.__index = Color3
function Color3.new(r, g, b)
	return setmetatable({ R = r or 0, G = g or 0, B = b or 0 }, Color3)
end
function Color3.fromRGB(r, g, b)
	return Color3.new((r or 0) / 255, (g or 0) / 255, (b or 0) / 255)
end

local loader = harness.new(sources, { Vector2 = Vector2, Color3 = Color3 })
local svg = loader.loadPackage("packages/svg/out")
local internal = svg.unstable_internal


local passed, failed = 0, 0
local failures = {}

local function check(name, ok, detail)
	if ok then
		passed += 1
	else
		failed += 1
		table.insert(failures, `{name}: {detail or "assertion failed"}`)
	end
end

local function equal(name, actual, expected)
	check(name, actual == expected, `expected {expected}, got {actual}`)
end

local function near(name, actual, expected, tolerance)
	local delta = math.abs(actual - expected)
	check(name, delta <= (tolerance or 1e-4), `expected ~{expected}, got {actual}`)
end

local function expectError(name, fn)
	local ok = pcall(fn)
	check(name, not ok, "expected an error, but the call succeeded")
end

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Base64 + header decoding
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

for name, fixture in fixtures.assets do
	local asset = internal.createAssetFromBase64(fixture.base64, fixture.hash)
	local data = internal.inspect(asset)

	equal(`{name}: byte length`, buffer.len(data.data), fixture.byteLength)
	equal(`{name}: shape count`, data.shapeCount, fixture.shapeCount)
	equal(`{name}: feature flags`, data.features, fixture.flags)
	near(`{name}: viewBox.x`, data.viewBox.x, fixture.viewBox.x)
	near(`{name}: viewBox.y`, data.viewBox.y, fixture.viewBox.y)
	near(`{name}: viewBox.width`, data.viewBox.width, fixture.viewBox.width)
	near(`{name}: viewBox.height`, data.viewBox.height, fixture.viewBox.height)
	equal(`{name}: id is the content hash`, data.id, fixture.hash)

	-- Public accessors agree with the internal view.
	equal(`{name}: getShapeCount`, svg.getShapeCount(asset), fixture.shapeCount)
	equal(`{name}: getFeatures`, svg.getFeatures(asset), fixture.flags)
	near(`{name}: getViewBox width`, svg.getViewBox(asset).width, fixture.viewBox.width)
end

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Lucide: the properties the whole design depends on
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

do
	local asset = internal.createAssetFromBase64(
		fixtures.assets.lucideSearch.base64,
		fixtures.assets.lucideSearch.hash
	)

	check("search is tintable", svg.isTintable(asset), "expected a tintable asset")
	equal("search shape count", svg.getShapeCount(asset), 2)

	local line = internal.shapeAt(asset, 0)
	check("search shape 0 has a stroke", line.hasStroke, "expected a stroke")
	check("search shape 0 has no fill", not line.hasFill, "Lucide sets fill=none")
	near("search stroke width", line.strokeWidth, 2)
	equal("search line cap is round", line.lineCap, 1)
	equal("search line join is round", line.lineJoin, 1)
	check("search fill rule is nonzero", not line.evenOdd, "expected nonzero")
	check("search paints fill first", not line.strokeFirst, "expected fill-then-stroke")

	local paint = internal.paintAt(asset, line.strokePaint)
	check("search stroke is currentColor", paint.isCurrentColor, "expected currentColor")
	near("search stroke alpha", paint.alpha, 1)

	-- The line is `m21 21-4.34-4.34`: a move followed by a single line.
	local ops = {}
	internal.visitCommands(asset, line, {
		-- roblox-ts emits colon-calls for interface methods, so each visitor
		-- receives the visitor table itself as its first argument.
		moveTo = function(_, x, y)
			table.insert(ops, { "moveTo", x, y })
		end,
		lineTo = function(_, x, y)
			table.insert(ops, { "lineTo", x, y })
		end,
		cubicTo = function(_, ...)
			table.insert(ops, { "cubicTo", ... })
		end,
		close = function()
			table.insert(ops, { "close" })
		end,
	})

	equal("search shape 0 command count", #ops, 2)
	equal("search shape 0 starts with a move", ops[1][1], "moveTo")
	near("search move x", ops[1][2], 21)
	near("search move y", ops[1][3], 21)
	equal("search shape 0 then lines", ops[2][1], "lineTo")
	near("search line x", ops[2][2], 16.66, 1e-2)
	near("search line y", ops[2][3], 16.66, 1e-2)

	-- The circle lowers to four cubic quadrants plus a close.
	local circle = internal.shapeAt(asset, 1)
	local cubics, closes = 0, 0
	internal.visitCommands(asset, circle, {
		moveTo = function() end,
		lineTo = function() end,
		cubicTo = function()
			cubics += 1
		end,
		close = function()
			closes += 1
		end,
	})
	equal("search circle cubic count", cubics, 4)
	equal("search circle close count", closes, 1)
end

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Paint, fill rule and coordinate space
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

do
	local asset = internal.createAssetFromBase64(fixtures.assets.solidFill.base64)
	local shape = internal.shapeAt(asset, 0)
	local paint = internal.paintAt(asset, shape.fillPaint)

	check("solid fill is not currentColor", not paint.isCurrentColor, "expected a solid colour")
	equal("solid fill red", paint.r, 0x33)
	equal("solid fill green", paint.g, 0x66)
	equal("solid fill blue", paint.b, 0x99)
	check("solid fill has no stroke", not shape.hasStroke, "expected no stroke")
	check("anonymous assets still get an id", internal.inspect(asset).id ~= nil, "missing id")
end

do
	local asset = internal.createAssetFromBase64(fixtures.assets.evenOdd.base64)
	check("evenodd survives the round trip", internal.shapeAt(asset, 0).evenOdd, "expected evenodd")
end

do
	-- Two subpaths means two moveTo commands; a decoder that dropped subpath
	-- structure would break fill rules.
	local asset = internal.createAssetFromBase64(fixtures.assets.multipleSubpaths.base64)
	local moves = 0
	internal.visitCommands(asset, internal.shapeAt(asset, 0), {
		moveTo = function()
			moves += 1
		end,
		lineTo = function() end,
		cubicTo = function() end,
		close = function() end,
	})
	equal("subpaths are preserved", moves, 2)
end

do
	-- The source declares width/height 96 with viewBox "-12 -12 24 24". The
	-- runtime must see the 24-unit space, with geometry around the origin.
	local asset = internal.createAssetFromBase64(fixtures.assets.offsetViewBox.base64)
	local viewBox = svg.getViewBox(asset)
	near("offset viewBox x", viewBox.x, -12)
	near("offset viewBox width", viewBox.width, 24)

	local minX, maxX = math.huge, -math.huge
	local function track(x)
		minX = math.min(minX, x)
		maxX = math.max(maxX, x)
	end
	internal.visitCommands(asset, internal.shapeAt(asset, 0), {
		moveTo = function(_, x)
			track(x)
		end,
		lineTo = function(_, x)
			track(x)
		end,
		cubicTo = function(_, c1x, _c1y, c2x, _c2y, x)
			track(c1x)
			track(c2x)
			track(x)
		end,
		close = function() end,
	})
	near("offset geometry min x", minX, -10, 0.05)
	near("offset geometry max x", maxX, 10, 0.05)
end

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Malformed input must error, never misbehave silently
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

expectError("empty payload is rejected", function()
	internal.createAssetFromBase64("")
end)

expectError("non-base64 payload is rejected", function()
	internal.createAssetFromBase64("!!!!")
end)

expectError("truncated payload is rejected", function()
	internal.createAssetFromBase64(string.sub(fixtures.assets.lucideSearch.base64, 1, 20))
end)

expectError("wrong magic is rejected", function()
	internal.createAssetFromBase64("AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA=")
end)

expectError("shape index out of range is rejected", function()
	local asset = internal.createAssetFromBase64(fixtures.assets.lucideSearch.base64)
	internal.shapeAt(asset, 99)
end)

expectError("paint index out of range is rejected", function()
	local asset = internal.createAssetFromBase64(fixtures.assets.lucideSearch.base64)
	internal.paintAt(asset, 99)
end)

-- Corrupted variants of a real header, so each rejection path is exercised for
-- the reason it exists rather than incidentally.
expectError("a future IR version is rejected", function()
	internal.createAssetFromBase64(fixtures.corrupt.wrongVersion)
end)

expectError("bad magic is rejected", function()
	internal.createAssetFromBase64(fixtures.corrupt.wrongMagic)
end)

expectError("tables larger than the blob are rejected", function()
	internal.createAssetFromBase64(fixtures.corrupt.overlongTables)
end)

expectError("a truncated header is rejected", function()
	internal.createAssetFromBase64(fixtures.corrupt.headerOnly)
end)

do
	-- The version error must name both versions, so the fix is obvious.
	local ok, message = pcall(function()
		internal.createAssetFromBase64(fixtures.corrupt.wrongVersion)
	end)
	check("version error is actionable", not ok and string.find(tostring(message), "Recompile") ~= nil,
		`message was {message}`)
end

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- preserveAspectRatio: the policy must survive compile -> IR -> Luau decode
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

do
	local ALIGN = svg.SvgAspectAlign
	local SCALE = svg.SvgAspectScale

	local cases = {
		-- fixture, expected align, expected scale, expected compiler string
		{ "aspectMeet", ALIGN.XMidYMid, SCALE.Meet, "xMidYMid meet" },
		{ "aspectNone", ALIGN.None, SCALE.Meet, "none" },
		{ "aspectSlice", ALIGN.XMinYMin, SCALE.Slice, "xMinYMin slice" },
		-- No attribute at all: SVG's default, which is *not* align 0.
		{ "lucideSearch", ALIGN.XMidYMid, SCALE.Meet, "xMidYMid meet" },
	}

	for _, case in cases do
		local name, expectedAlign, expectedScale, expectedText = case[1], case[2], case[3], case[4]
		local fixture = fixtures.assets[name]
		local asset = internal.createAssetFromBase64(fixture.base64, fixture.hash)
		local aspect = svg.getPreserveAspectRatio(asset)

		equal(`{name}: aspect align`, aspect.align, expectedAlign)
		equal(`{name}: aspect scale`, aspect.scale, expectedScale)
		-- The compiler's own rendering of the same value, so the two halves of
		-- the pipeline are checked against each other and not just internally.
		equal(`{name}: compiler agrees`, fixture.preserveAspectRatio, expectedText)
	end
end

do
	-- The three aspect fixtures share their geometry and their view box, so the
	-- fitting transform is the only thing that can tell them apart. This is
	-- exactly the information IR version 1 discarded.
	local function fit(name, width, height)
		local fixture = fixtures.assets[name]
		local asset = internal.createAssetFromBase64(fixture.base64)
		return svg.viewBoxTransform(
			svg.getViewBox(asset),
			svg.getPreserveAspectRatio(asset),
			width,
			height
		)
	end

	local function mapPoint(t, x, y)
		return t.sx * x + t.kx * y + t.tx, t.ky * x + t.sy * y + t.ty
	end

	-- 24x12 letterboxed into 100x100 becomes 100x50, centred vertically.
	local meet = fit("aspectMeet", 100, 100)
	local x, y = mapPoint(meet, 0, 0)
	near("meet: origin x", x, 0)
	near("meet: origin y", y, 25)
	x, y = mapPoint(meet, 24, 12)
	near("meet: far corner x", x, 100)
	near("meet: far corner y", y, 75)

	-- `none` stretches: the view box corner lands on the target corner.
	local none = fit("aspectNone", 100, 100)
	x, y = mapPoint(none, 24, 12)
	near("none: far corner x", x, 100)
	near("none: far corner y", y, 100)
	near("none: scales differ", none.sx / none.sy, 100 / 24 / (100 / 12))

	-- `slice` from the top-left covers the target at 200x100 and crops.
	local slice = fit("aspectSlice", 100, 100)
	x, y = mapPoint(slice, 0, 0)
	near("slice: origin x", x, 0)
	near("slice: origin y", y, 0)
	x, y = mapPoint(slice, 24, 12)
	near("slice: far corner x", x, 200)
	near("slice: far corner y", y, 100)

	-- A non-zero view box origin must land on the aligned corner.
	local offset = fixtures.assets.offsetViewBox
	local offsetAsset = internal.createAssetFromBase64(offset.base64)
	local t = svg.viewBoxTransform(
		svg.getViewBox(offsetAsset),
		svg.getPreserveAspectRatio(offsetAsset),
		48,
		48
	)
	x, y = mapPoint(t, -12, -12)
	near("offset viewBox origin maps to the target origin x", x, 0)
	near("offset viewBox origin maps to the target origin y", y, 0)
end

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Sizing: layout size and raster resolution are different things
--
-- This policy lives in the core rather than in a binding because React and
-- Vide have to answer it identically; testing it here, with no component
-- mounted, is the point of it being separable.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

do
	local viewBox = { x = 0, y = 0, width = 24, height = 12 }

	-- Explicit numeric `size`: known up front, so nothing has to be measured.
	local numeric = svg.resolveSvgSizing(viewBox, 24, false)
	check("numeric size needs no measurement", not numeric.measureAbsoluteSize, "expected false")
	equal("numeric size raster width", numeric.declaredPixels.X, 24)
	equal("numeric size raster height", numeric.declaredPixels.Y, 24)

	-- `Size` alone: the raster resolution comes from AbsoluteSize.
	local robloxSize = svg.resolveSvgSizing(viewBox, nil, true)
	check("Size is measured", robloxSize.measureAbsoluteSize, "expected true")

	-- Both: `Size` wins, so the raster still follows AbsoluteSize. This is the
	-- bug that let `<Svg source={Search} Size={UDim2.fromOffset(96, 96)} />`
	-- rasterize at 24x24 and then stretch the result.
	local both = svg.resolveSvgSizing(viewBox, 24, true)
	check("Size wins over size", both.measureAbsoluteSize, "expected Size to take precedence")

	-- Neither: the view box's own dimensions.
	local intrinsic = svg.resolveSvgSizing(viewBox, nil, false)
	check("intrinsic needs no measurement", not intrinsic.measureAbsoluteSize, "expected false")
	equal("intrinsic width", intrinsic.declaredPixels.X, 24)
	equal("intrinsic height", intrinsic.declaredPixels.Y, 12)

	-- Snapping is what stops a resizing layout rasterizing every frame, and the
	-- 1x1 floor is what stops it producing an invalid EditableImage.
	equal("snap rounds up", svg.snapSvgPixelSize(Vector2.new(23.6, 23.6)).X, 24)
	equal("snap rounds down", svg.snapSvgPixelSize(Vector2.new(24.4, 24.4)).X, 24)
	equal("snap floors at one pixel", svg.snapSvgPixelSize(Vector2.new(0, 0)).X, 1)
	equal("snap floors negatives too", svg.snapSvgPixelSize(Vector2.new(-5, -5)).Y, 1)
end

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- No renderer installed: fail fast, before anything installs one
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

do
	local asset = internal.createAssetFromBase64(fixtures.assets.lucideSearch.base64)
	check(
		"no renderer is installed yet",
		svg.getSvgRenderer() == nil,
		"a renderer was installed before this test"
	)

	local ok, message = pcall(function()
		svg.renderSvg(asset, { size = Vector2.new(24, 24) })
	end)
	check("renderSvg throws when no renderer is installed", not ok, "expected an error")
	check(
		"the no-renderer error names setSvgRenderer",
		not ok and string.find(tostring(message), "setSvgRenderer", 1, true) ~= nil,
		`message was {message}`
	)
end

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Render cache: keys, sharing and deterministic release
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

do
	local asset = internal.createAssetFromBase64(
		fixtures.assets.lucideSearch.base64,
		fixtures.assets.lucideSearch.hash
	)

	local rendered, destroyed = 0, 0
	local fakeRenderer = {
		version = 1,
		render = function()
			rendered += 1
			return { id = rendered }
		end,
		destroy = function()
			destroyed += 1
		end,
	}

	svg.setSvgRenderer(fakeRenderer)

	local a = svg.renderSvg(asset, { size = Vector2.new(24, 24) })
	local b = svg.renderSvg(asset, { size = Vector2.new(24, 24) })
	equal("identical requests rasterize once", rendered, 1)
	equal("identical requests share an image", a.image, b.image)
	check("handle reports tintable", a.tintable, "search is tintable")

	local c = svg.renderSvg(asset, { size = Vector2.new(48, 48) })
	equal("a different size rasterizes again", rendered, 2)
	check("a different size is a different image", c.image ~= a.image, "images should differ")

	a.release()
	equal("image survives while referenced", destroyed, 0)
	a.release()
	equal("releasing twice does not double free", destroyed, 0)
	b.release()
	equal("last release destroys the image", destroyed, 1)

	c.release()
	equal("all images released", destroyed, 2)
	equal("cache is empty", svg.getSvgRenderCache():stats().entryCount, 0)

	-- Sub-pixel sizes must snap, or an animated size would miss every frame.
	local d = svg.renderSvg(asset, { size = Vector2.new(24.4, 23.6) })
	local e = svg.renderSvg(asset, { size = Vector2.new(24, 24) })
	equal("fractional sizes snap to the same entry", d.image, e.image)
	d.release()
	e.release()

	-- Colour is deliberately absent from the key for tintable assets, which is
	-- what the whole ImageColor3 fast path relies on. Nothing in the options
	-- carries a colour, so this is structural: assert the key's shape.
	local resolved = svg.resolveRenderOptions(asset, { size = Vector2.new(24, 24) })
	local key = svg.renderCacheKey(asset, resolved, 1)
	check(
		"cache key contains the asset hash",
		string.find(key, fixtures.assets.lucideSearch.hash, 1, true) ~= nil,
		`key was {key}`
	)
	check("cache key contains the pixel size", string.find(key, "24x24", 1, true) ~= nil, key)
	check("cache key contains the renderer version", string.find(key, "r1", 1, true) ~= nil, key)
end

do
	-- Absolute stroke width is specified in pixels and must be converted into
	-- view box units, so it produces a different key at a different size.
	local asset = internal.createAssetFromBase64(fixtures.assets.lucideSearch.base64)
	local atSmall = svg.resolveRenderOptions(
		asset,
		{ size = Vector2.new(24, 24), strokeWidth = 2, absoluteStrokeWidth = true }
	)
	local atLarge = svg.resolveRenderOptions(
		asset,
		{ size = Vector2.new(48, 48), strokeWidth = 2, absoluteStrokeWidth = true }
	)
	near("absolute stroke at 1x", atSmall.strokeWidth, 2)
	near("absolute stroke at 2x halves in view box units", atLarge.strokeWidth, 1)

	local relative = svg.resolveRenderOptions(
		asset,
		{ size = Vector2.new(48, 48), strokeWidth = 2 }
	)
	near("relative stroke is unchanged by size", relative.strokeWidth, 2)
end

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Colour paths: the three asset classes and their cache keys
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

do
	local function assetOf(name)
		local fixture = fixtures.assets[name]
		return internal.createAssetFromBase64(fixture.base64, fixture.hash)
	end

	local fixed = assetOf("solidFill")
	local tintable = assetOf("lucideSearch")
	local mixed = assetOf("mixedCurrentColor")

	-- The feature helper that decides the paths.
	check("usesCurrentColor: fixed-colour asset", not svg.usesCurrentColor(fixed), "expected false")
	check("usesCurrentColor: tintable asset", svg.usesCurrentColor(tintable), "expected true")
	check("usesCurrentColor: mixed asset", svg.usesCurrentColor(mixed), "expected true")
	check("isTintable: mixed asset is NOT tintable", not svg.isTintable(mixed),
		"mixed currentColor must never take the ImageColor3 path")

	-- resolveRenderOptions carries a concrete colour, defaulting to black.
	local resolved = svg.resolveRenderOptions(tintable, { size = Vector2.new(24, 24) })
	check(
		"resolve: currentColor defaults to black",
		resolved.currentColor.R == 0 and resolved.currentColor.G == 0 and resolved.currentColor.B == 0,
		`got {resolved.currentColor.R},{resolved.currentColor.G},{resolved.currentColor.B}`
	)

	local rendered = 0
	local seenColors = {}
	svg.setSvgRenderer({
		version = 1,
		render = function(_, _, options)
			rendered += 1
			table.insert(seenColors, options.currentColor)
			return { id = rendered }
		end,
		destroy = function() end,
	})

	local red = Color3.fromRGB(255, 0, 0)
	local blue = Color3.fromRGB(0, 0, 255)
	local white = Color3.fromRGB(255, 255, 255)

	-- Case A: no currentColor in the asset. The requested colour cannot
	-- change a pixel, so every colour hits one cache entry.
	local a1 = svg.renderSvg(fixed, { size = Vector2.new(24, 24), currentColor = red })
	local a2 = svg.renderSvg(fixed, { size = Vector2.new(24, 24), currentColor = blue })
	local a3 = svg.renderSvg(fixed, { size = Vector2.new(24, 24) })
	equal("case A: colour never re-rasterizes a fixed-colour asset", rendered, 1)
	check("case A: all colours share one image", a1.image == a2.image and a2.image == a3.image, "images differ")
	check("case A: the key carries no colour", string.find(a1.cacheKey, "|c", 1, true) == nil, a1.cacheKey)

	-- Case B: tintable. One shared alpha mask; ImageColor3 does the colour.
	rendered = 0
	local b1 = svg.renderSvg(tintable, { size = Vector2.new(24, 24), currentColor = red })
	local b2 = svg.renderSvg(tintable, { size = Vector2.new(24, 24), currentColor = blue })
	local b3 = svg.renderSvg(tintable, { size = Vector2.new(24, 24), currentColor = white })
	equal("case B: three colours of one Lucide icon rasterize once", rendered, 1)
	check("case B: three colours share one image", b1.image == b2.image and b2.image == b3.image, "images differ")
	check("case B: handles report tintable", b1.tintable, "expected tintable")
	check("case B: the key carries no colour", string.find(b1.cacheKey, "|c", 1, true) == nil, b1.cacheKey)

	-- Case C: mixed. The resolved colour reaches the compositor, so it is
	-- part of the identity.
	rendered = 0
	seenColors = {}
	local c1 = svg.renderSvg(mixed, { size = Vector2.new(24, 24), currentColor = red })
	local c2 = svg.renderSvg(mixed, { size = Vector2.new(24, 24), currentColor = blue })
	equal("case C: two colours of a mixed asset rasterize twice", rendered, 2)
	check("case C: two colours are two images", c1.image ~= c2.image, "images shared")
	check("case C: keys differ by colour", c1.cacheKey ~= c2.cacheKey, c1.cacheKey)
	check("case C: the key carries the colour", string.find(c1.cacheKey, "|c255,0,0", 1, true) ~= nil, c1.cacheKey)
	check("case C: handles are not tintable", not c1.tintable, "mixed asset claimed tintable")
	check(
		"case C: the renderer received the resolved colour",
		seenColors[1] ~= nil and seenColors[1].R == 1 and seenColors[1].B == 0,
		"resolved colour missing"
	)

	-- Value semantics: a *different Color3 object* with the same channels must
	-- share the entry, and the default must equal explicit black.
	local c3 = svg.renderSvg(mixed, { size = Vector2.new(24, 24), currentColor = Color3.fromRGB(255, 0, 0) })
	equal("case C: an equal colour value reuses the raster", rendered, 2)
	check("case C: equal colour values share the image", c1.image == c3.image, "images differ")

	local d1 = svg.renderSvg(mixed, { size = Vector2.new(24, 24) })
	local d2 = svg.renderSvg(mixed, { size = Vector2.new(24, 24), currentColor = Color3.new(0, 0, 0) })
	check("case C: omitted colour equals explicit black", d1.image == d2.image, "default drifted from black")

	for _, handle in { a1, a2, a3, b1, b2, b3, c1, c2, c3, d1, d2 } do
		handle.release()
	end
	equal("colour paths: everything released", svg.getSvgRenderCache():stats().entryCount, 0)
end

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

print(`luau: {passed} passed, {failed} failed`)
for _, failure in failures do
	print("  FAIL " .. failure)
end
if failed > 0 then
	error(`{failed} Luau assertion(s) failed`, 0)
end



================================================
FILE: tests/luau/vide-loader.luau
================================================
--!nocheck
--[[
	Loads the real `@rbxts/vide` into a mocked Roblox environment.

	Vide is a pure Luau library — its only engine dependencies are instance
	creation, a handful of datatypes and `typeof` — which is what makes running
	the actual reactive library here possible, and worth doing. A hand-written
	stand-in for `source`/`effect`/`cleanup` would agree with whatever the
	binding happened to do; the real one has opinions about scope ownership,
	cleanup ordering and strict-mode double evaluation that the binding has to
	be correct against.

	Its modules require each other by relative path (`require "./graph"`), which
	the CLI resolves against a real file on disk. These are embedded strings, so
	they are given a `require` of their own that resolves the same names out of
	the bundle. `../test/mock` never resolves, and never needs to: it is Vide's
	fallback for running without a `game`, and here there is one.
]]

local videSources = require("./vide-sources")

--[[
	Returns a freshly loaded Vide.

	Fresh per call because Vide keeps process-wide state — the scope stack, the
	update queue, the strict-mode flag — and a suite that toggles strict mode
	should not leak that into the next one.

	@param globals the base environment, from `roblox.globals()`.
]]
return function(globals)
	local baseGlobals = setmetatable(globals, { __index = getfenv(1) })
	local loaded = {}

	local function videRequire(path)
		local name = string.match(path, "([^/]+)$")
		if loaded[name] ~= nil then
			return loaded[name]
		end

		local source = videSources[name]
		if source == nil then
			error(`@rbxts/vide has no module {path}`, 0)
		end

		local chunk, compileError = loadstring(source, `@vide/{name}`)
		if chunk == nil then
			error(`failed to compile vide/{name}: {compileError}`, 0)
		end

		setfenv(chunk, setmetatable({ require = videRequire }, { __index = baseGlobals }))

		local result = chunk()
		loaded[name] = result
		return result
	end

	-- `lib` rather than `init`: `init.luau` is the Roblox entry point and
	-- resolves its siblings through `script`, which does not exist here. Vide's
	-- own assertion in that file points at `lib` for exactly this case.
	return videRequire("./lib")
end



================================================
FILE: tests/luau/vide.luau
================================================
--!nocheck
--[[
	Lifecycle and reactivity tests for `@rbxts/svg-vide`.

	These run the *compiled* binding — the Luau `rbxtsc` emitted — against the
	*real* `@rbxts/vide`, with only Roblox datatypes and instances mocked. That
	combination is the point. A stand-in reactive library would agree with
	whatever the binding happened to do; the real one has opinions the binding
	has to be correct against:

	- a scope's cleanups are flushed *before* it reruns, not after;
	- strict mode evaluates every reactive scope twice on purpose;
	- a source only notifies when its new value differs from the old one.

	What is deliberately not tested here is anything about pixels. Flattening,
	stroke expansion, coverage and compositing belong to the core and are
	covered by `spec.luau` and `raster.luau` against the Rust reference. A
	framework binding's job is which requests reach the renderer and when the
	results are let go of, so that is all this file asserts.

	Run with `pnpm test:luau`, which regenerates the bundle first.
]]

local harness = require("./harness")
local sources = require("./sources")
local fixtures = require("./fixtures")
local roblox = require("./roblox")
local loadVide = require("./vide-loader")

local Vector2 = roblox.Vector2
local Color3 = roblox.Color3
local UDim2 = roblox.UDim2
local Content = roblox.Content

local vide = loadVide(roblox.globals())

-- Filled in as each package loads. `@rbxts/svg` is registered before the
-- binding is loaded, so the binding's `TS.getModule(script, "@rbxts", "svg")`
-- resolves to *this* core instance: one core, one cache, which is the
-- invariant the cross-framework test below depends on.
local packages = { ["@rbxts/vide"] = vide }
local loader = harness.new(sources, roblox.globals(), packages)

local svg = loader.loadPackage("packages/svg/out")
packages["@rbxts/svg"] = svg

local svgVide = loader.loadPackage("packages/svg-vide/out")
local Svg = svgVide.Svg
local internal = svg.unstable_internal

local passed, failed = 0, 0
local failures = {}

local function check(name, ok, detail)
	if ok then
		passed += 1
	else
		failed += 1
		table.insert(failures, `{name}: {detail or "assertion failed"}`)
	end
end

local function equal(name, actual, expected)
	check(name, actual == expected, `expected {expected}, got {actual}`)
end

local function asset(fixtureName)
	local fixture = fixtures.assets[fixtureName]
	return internal.createAssetFromBase64(fixture.base64, fixture.hash)
end

-- `search` is the Lucide shape of asset: monochrome currentColor, so tintable.
-- `mixedCurrentColor` mixes currentColor with fixed paints, so its colour is
-- geometry. `solidFill` has no currentColor at all. Those three classes are
-- what every colour assertion below is really about.
local SEARCH = asset("lucideSearch")
local SETTINGS = asset("lucideSettings")
local MIXED = asset("mixedCurrentColor")
local FIXED = asset("solidFill")

check("search is tintable", svg.isTintable(SEARCH), "fixture assumption")
check("mixed uses currentColor", svg.usesCurrentColor(MIXED), "fixture assumption")
check("mixed is not tintable", not svg.isTintable(MIXED), "fixture assumption")
check("fixed has no currentColor", not svg.usesCurrentColor(FIXED), "fixture assumption")

--[[
	A renderer that records what it was asked for, in order.

	The order is as important as the count: the binding is required to acquire a
	new raster *before* releasing the old one, and the only way to see that from
	outside is that no image is destroyed between the two.
]]
local function newRenderer()
	local renderer = { version = 1, images = {}, destroyed = {}, events = {} }

	-- Colon-called: roblox-ts emits `self.renderer:render(...)` for an interface
	-- method, so each implementation receives the renderer itself first.
	renderer.render = function(_, _asset, options)
		local image = {
			index = #renderer.images + 1,
			width = options.pixelWidth,
			height = options.pixelHeight,
			strokeWidth = options.strokeWidth,
			currentColor = options.currentColor,
		}
		table.insert(renderer.images, image)
		table.insert(renderer.events, `render {image.width}x{image.height}#{image.index}`)
		return image
	end

	renderer.destroy = function(_, image)
		table.insert(renderer.destroyed, image)
		table.insert(renderer.events, `destroy {image.width}x{image.height}#{image.index}`)
	end

	return renderer
end

--[[
	Installs a fresh renderer and returns it plus the cache behind it.

	`setSvgRenderer` clears the cache, so each scenario starts with no entries
	and no outstanding references regardless of what the previous one left.
]]
local function newScenario()
	local renderer = newRenderer()
	svg.setSvgRenderer(renderer)
	return renderer, svg.getSvgRenderCache()
end

local function stats(cache)
	return cache:stats()
end

-- Strict mode is Vide's development aid: it runs every reactive scope twice to
-- surface scopes that are not idempotent. It is off for the counting tests
-- because doubled evaluations would make every count ambiguous, and gets its
-- own scenario at the end where the doubling is the thing under test.
vide.strict = false

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- No renderer installed
--
-- First, because there is no way back to "no renderer" once one is installed —
-- and because it is the state a real application is in until it calls
-- `installEditableImageRenderer()`.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

do
	-- The same failure React gets, for the same reason: a missing renderer is a
	-- configuration error, and an icon that silently renders as nothing is far
	-- harder to diagnose than one that fails at startup.
	check("no renderer is installed yet", svg.getSvgRenderer() == nil, "one was installed early")

	local ok, message = pcall(function()
		vide.root(function()
			return Svg({ source = SEARCH, size = 24 })
		end)
	end)

	check("mounting without a renderer fails", not ok, "expected an error")
	check(
		"and the error is the core's actionable one",
		not ok and string.find(tostring(message), "installEditableImageRenderer", 1, true) ~= nil,
		`message was {message}`
	)
end

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- A static mount
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

do
	local renderer, cache = newScenario()
	local white = Color3.fromRGB(255, 255, 255)

	local destroy, label = vide.root(function()
		return Svg({ source = SEARCH, size = 24, color = white })
	end)

	equal("static mount rasterizes once", #renderer.images, 1)
	equal("static mount raster width", renderer.images[1].width, 24)
	equal("static mount raster height", renderer.images[1].height, 24)
	equal("static mount layout size", label.Size, UDim2.fromOffset(24, 24))
	equal("static mount shows the raster", label.ImageContent, Content.fromObject(renderer.images[1]))
	equal("static mount tints with the colour", label.ImageColor3, white)
	equal("static mount is transparent behind", label.BackgroundTransparency, 1)
	equal("static mount creates an ImageLabel", label.ClassName, "ImageLabel")

	-- The SVG-specific props are consumed, not forwarded: Vide assigns every
	-- string key of a props table onto the instance, so a leaked `source` would
	-- show up here as a property (and in the engine as an error).
	equal("source is not forwarded to the instance", label.source, nil)
	equal("size is not forwarded to the instance", label.size, nil)
	equal("color is not forwarded to the instance", label.color, nil)

	local before = stats(cache)
	equal("static mount holds one entry", before.entryCount, 1)
	equal("static mount holds one reference", before.referenceCount, 1)

	destroy()

	local after = stats(cache)
	equal("destroying the scope releases the entry", after.entryCount, 0)
	equal("destroying the scope releases the reference", after.referenceCount, 0)
	equal("destroying the scope destroys the image", #renderer.destroyed, 1)
end

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- A reactive numeric size
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

do
	local renderer, cache = newScenario()
	local size = vide.source(24)

	local destroy, label = vide.root(function()
		return Svg({ source = SEARCH, size = size })
	end)

	equal("reactive size starts at 24", renderer.images[1].width, 24)
	equal("reactive size lays out at 24", label.Size, UDim2.fromOffset(24, 24))

	size(48)

	equal("changing size rasterizes again", #renderer.images, 2)
	equal("the new raster is the new size", renderer.images[2].width, 48)
	equal("the layout follows too", label.Size, UDim2.fromOffset(48, 48))
	equal("the label shows the new raster", label.ImageContent, Content.fromObject(renderer.images[2]))

	-- The ordering rule: acquire, publish, *then* release. A release-first
	-- binding would emit destroy before render here, and would destroy an image
	-- another component might have been about to reuse.
	equal("the new raster is acquired first", renderer.events[2], "render 48x48#2")
	equal("the old raster is released after", renderer.events[3], "destroy 24x24#1")

	local live = stats(cache)
	equal("only the current size is cached", live.entryCount, 1)
	equal("only one reference is held", live.referenceCount, 1)

	destroy()
	equal("every raster is destroyed exactly once", #renderer.destroyed, 2)
	equal("nothing is left referenced", stats(cache).referenceCount, 0)
end

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Colour, by asset class
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

do
	-- Tintable: the raster is a shared alpha mask, so colour is an ImageColor3
	-- write and nothing else. This is the Lucide fast path, and the single most
	-- important thing for the binding not to get wrong.
	local renderer, cache = newScenario()
	local colour = vide.source(Color3.fromRGB(255, 255, 255))

	local destroy, label = vide.root(function()
		return Svg({ source = SEARCH, size = 24, color = colour })
	end)

	equal("tintable mount rasterizes once", #renderer.images, 1)

	colour(Color3.fromRGB(0, 0, 255))
	equal("recolouring a tintable asset does not rasterize", #renderer.images, 1)
	equal("recolouring a tintable asset updates the tint", label.ImageColor3, Color3.fromRGB(0, 0, 255))

	colour(Color3.fromRGB(0, 255, 0))
	equal("recolouring again still does not rasterize", #renderer.images, 1)
	equal("recolouring again updates the tint", label.ImageColor3, Color3.fromRGB(0, 255, 0))
	equal("no raster was ever destroyed", #renderer.destroyed, 0)
	equal("the one entry is still the one entry", stats(cache).entryCount, 1)

	destroy()
end

do
	-- Mixed currentColor: the colour reaches the compositor, so each distinct
	-- colour genuinely is a different picture and a different cache entry.
	local renderer, cache = newScenario()
	local colour = vide.source(Color3.fromRGB(255, 0, 0))

	local destroy, label = vide.root(function()
		return Svg({ source = MIXED, size = 24, color = colour })
	end)

	equal("mixed mount rasterizes once", #renderer.images, 1)
	equal(
		"mixed mount passes the colour through",
		renderer.images[1].currentColor,
		Color3.fromRGB(255, 0, 0)
	)
	equal("mixed assets are not tinted by ImageColor3", label.ImageColor3, Color3.new(1, 1, 1))

	colour(Color3.fromRGB(0, 0, 255))
	equal("recolouring a mixed asset rasterizes again", #renderer.images, 2)
	equal(
		"the new raster has the new colour",
		renderer.images[2].currentColor,
		Color3.fromRGB(0, 0, 255)
	)
	equal("the previous raster is released", #renderer.destroyed, 1)
	equal("and it was the first one", renderer.destroyed[1].index, 1)
	equal("mixed assets are still not tinted", label.ImageColor3, Color3.new(1, 1, 1))
	equal("only the current colour is cached", stats(cache).entryCount, 1)

	destroy()
end

do
	-- No currentColor at all: `color` cannot change a single pixel, and must
	-- not be quietly promoted into a blanket image tint either.
	local renderer = newScenario()
	local colour = vide.source(Color3.fromRGB(255, 0, 0))

	local destroy, label = vide.root(function()
		return Svg({ source = FIXED, size = 24, color = colour })
	end)

	equal("fixed-colour mount rasterizes once", #renderer.images, 1)
	equal("a fixed-colour asset is not tinted", label.ImageColor3, Color3.new(1, 1, 1))

	colour(Color3.fromRGB(0, 0, 255))
	equal("recolouring a fixed-colour asset does not rasterize", #renderer.images, 1)
	equal("recolouring a fixed-colour asset does not tint", label.ImageColor3, Color3.new(1, 1, 1))

	destroy()
end

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Sharing: one raster, many labels — and many frameworks
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

do
	local renderer, cache = newScenario()

	local destroy = vide.root(function()
		return {
			Svg({ source = SEARCH, size = 24, color = Color3.fromRGB(255, 0, 0) }),
			Svg({ source = SEARCH, size = 24, color = Color3.fromRGB(0, 0, 255) }),
		}
	end)

	equal("two colours of one tintable icon rasterize once", #renderer.images, 1)
	equal("they share one cache entry", stats(cache).entryCount, 1)
	equal("held by two references", stats(cache).referenceCount, 2)

	destroy()
	equal("and the image survives until the last one goes", #renderer.destroyed, 1)
end

do
	-- The cross-framework invariant, at the lowest layer it can be stated:
	-- `renderSvg` is exactly what `@rbxts/svg-react`'s `useSvg` calls, so a
	-- direct call here is a React tree's request. Nothing about the framework is
	-- in the cache key, so the two share an entry and an EditableImage.
	local renderer, cache = newScenario()

	local reactHandle = svg.renderSvg(SEARCH, {
		size = Vector2.new(24, 24),
		currentColor = Color3.fromRGB(255, 0, 0),
	})

	local destroy, label = vide.root(function()
		return Svg({ source = SEARCH, size = 24, color = Color3.fromRGB(0, 0, 255) })
	end)

	equal("a React request and a Vide component rasterize once", #renderer.images, 1)
	equal("they share one cache entry", stats(cache).entryCount, 1)
	equal("held by two references", stats(cache).referenceCount, 2)
	equal("and it is literally the same image", label.ImageContent, Content.fromObject(reactHandle.image))

	destroy()
	equal("destroying the Vide scope does not destroy React's image", #renderer.destroyed, 0)
	reactHandle:release()
	equal("the last release does", #renderer.destroyed, 1)
end

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- A Roblox-native `Size`
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

do
	local renderer = newScenario()

	local destroy, label = vide.root(function()
		return Svg({ source = SEARCH, Size = UDim2.fromOffset(64, 32) })
	end)

	equal("the UDim2 is used verbatim for layout", label.Size, UDim2.fromOffset(64, 32))
	-- Layout has not run, so the only honest answer is the smallest valid image.
	-- Rasterizing at the view box size instead would be a *wrong* resolution
	-- rather than an unknown one.
	equal("before layout the raster is 1x1", renderer.images[1].width, 1)

	label.AbsoluteSize = Vector2.new(64, 32)

	equal("layout drives a new raster", #renderer.images, 2)
	equal("at the laid-out width", renderer.images[2].width, 64)
	equal("at the laid-out height", renderer.images[2].height, 32)
	equal("and the placeholder is released", #renderer.destroyed, 1)

	destroy()
end

do
	-- A scale-based UDim2 cannot be turned into pixels at all without layout,
	-- which is the whole reason the measurement exists.
	local renderer = newScenario()

	local destroy, label = vide.root(function()
		return Svg({ source = SEARCH, Size = UDim2.fromScale(0.5, 0.25) })
	end)

	label.AbsoluteSize = Vector2.new(100, 50)

	equal("a scale Size rasters at the resolved size", renderer.images[#renderer.images].width, 100)
	equal("in both dimensions", renderer.images[#renderer.images].height, 50)

	destroy()
end

do
	-- Both props: `Size` wins, so the raster follows AbsoluteSize and not the 24
	-- that `size` asked for. This is the precedence React documents.
	local renderer = newScenario()

	local destroy, label = vide.root(function()
		return Svg({ source = SEARCH, size = 24, Size = UDim2.fromOffset(96, 96) })
	end)

	label.AbsoluteSize = Vector2.new(96, 96)

	equal("Size wins over size", renderer.images[#renderer.images].width, 96)

	destroy()
end

do
	-- Subpixel layout noise must not reach the renderer: two AbsoluteSizes that
	-- round to the same integers are the same raster. Without this, an animated
	-- layout rasterizes on every frame it moves at all.
	local renderer = newScenario()

	local destroy, label = vide.root(function()
		return Svg({ source = SEARCH, Size = UDim2.fromScale(1, 1) })
	end)

	label.AbsoluteSize = Vector2.new(47.8, 48.2)
	local afterFirst = #renderer.images
	equal("a fractional size snaps to whole pixels", renderer.images[afterFirst].width, 48)
	equal("in both dimensions", renderer.images[afterFirst].height, 48)

	label.AbsoluteSize = Vector2.new(48.2, 47.8)
	equal("a size that snaps the same does not rasterize", #renderer.images, afterFirst)

	label.AbsoluteSize = Vector2.new(48, 48)
	equal("nor does landing exactly on it", #renderer.images, afterFirst)

	destroy()
end

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- A reactive asset
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

do
	local renderer, cache = newScenario()
	local icon = vide.source(SEARCH)

	local destroy, label = vide.root(function()
		return Svg({ source = icon, size = 24 })
	end)

	equal("a reactive source mounts", #renderer.images, 1)

	icon(SETTINGS)

	equal("swapping the asset rasterizes the new one", #renderer.images, 2)
	equal("the new raster is acquired first", renderer.events[2], "render 24x24#2")
	equal("the old one is released after", renderer.events[3], "destroy 24x24#1")
	equal("the label shows the new asset", label.ImageContent, Content.fromObject(renderer.images[2]))
	equal("only one entry is live", stats(cache).entryCount, 1)

	destroy()
end

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Stroke width
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

do
	local renderer = newScenario()
	local width = vide.source(2)

	local destroy = vide.root(function()
		return Svg({ source = SEARCH, size = 24, strokeWidth = width })
	end)

	equal("the stroke override reaches the renderer", renderer.images[1].strokeWidth, 2)

	width(1)
	equal("changing it rasterizes again", #renderer.images, 2)
	equal("with the new width", renderer.images[2].strokeWidth, 1)

	destroy()
end

do
	-- `absoluteStrokeWidth` is a unit, and converting it is the core's job:
	-- 2 pixels at 48px on a 24-unit view box is 1 view box unit. The binding
	-- must pass the flag through rather than doing arithmetic of its own.
	local renderer = newScenario()

	local destroy = vide.root(function()
		return Svg({ source = SEARCH, size = 48, strokeWidth = 2, absoluteStrokeWidth = true })
	end)

	equal("an absolute stroke is converted to view box units", renderer.images[1].strokeWidth, 1)

	destroy()
end

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Conditional scopes
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

do
	-- Destroying the whole root proves little on its own: the interesting case
	-- is a branch scope disappearing while the application keeps running, which
	-- is what `show` (and `<Show>`) creates.
	local renderer, cache = newScenario()
	local visible = vide.source(true)

	local destroy = vide.root(function()
		return vide.jsx(
			"frame",
			{},
			vide.show(visible, function()
				return Svg({ source = SEARCH, size = 24 })
			end)
		)
	end)

	equal("the branch mounts", stats(cache).referenceCount, 1)

	visible(false)
	equal("hiding the branch releases the handle", stats(cache).referenceCount, 0)
	equal("and destroys the raster", #renderer.destroyed, 1)

	visible(true)
	equal("showing it again acquires a new one", stats(cache).referenceCount, 1)
	equal("rasterizing again", #renderer.images, 2)

	destroy()
	equal("nothing is left over", stats(cache).referenceCount, 0)
	equal("every raster is destroyed exactly once", #renderer.destroyed, 2)
end

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Lifecycle counters
--
-- Not a raster benchmark — those belong to the core and are measured against
-- the Rust reference. These count the thing a framework binding can get wrong
-- at scale: how many times a run of updates reaches the rasterizer.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

do
	local renderer, cache = newScenario()
	local colour = vide.source(Color3.fromRGB(0, 0, 0))

	local destroy, label = vide.root(function()
		return Svg({ source = SEARCH, size = 24, color = colour })
	end)

	equal("mounting costs one raster", #renderer.images, 1)

	-- A theme animation, or a hundred frames of a colour tween.
	for step = 1, 100 do
		colour(Color3.fromRGB(step * 2 % 256, 255 - step % 256, step % 256))
	end

	equal("100 tint-only updates cost none", #renderer.images, 1)
	equal("and free nothing", #renderer.destroyed, 0)
	equal("and still hold one reference", stats(cache).referenceCount, 1)
	equal("with the last colour applied", label.ImageColor3, Color3.fromRGB(200, 155, 100))

	destroy()
end

do
	local renderer, cache = newScenario()
	local size = vide.source(16)

	local destroy = vide.root(function()
		return Svg({ source = SEARCH, size = size })
	end)

	-- 16 → 24 → 32 → 24. The last step is the interesting one: its raster was
	-- freed when nothing referenced it, so returning costs a rasterization
	-- rather than a hit. That is the current cache policy — an entry lives
	-- exactly as long as something holds it — and a future size-bounded cache
	-- that retains unreferenced entries would turn this into a hit without the
	-- binding changing at all.
	for _, target in { 24, 32, 24 } do
		size(target)
	end

	equal("a four-step size sequence costs four rasters", #renderer.images, 4)
	equal("three of which are freed on the way", #renderer.destroyed, 3)
	equal("leaving one entry", stats(cache).entryCount, 1)
	equal("and one reference", stats(cache).referenceCount, 1)

	destroy()
	equal("and nothing at the end", stats(cache).entryCount, 0)
	equal("with every raster destroyed exactly once", #renderer.destroyed, #renderer.images)
end

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Strict mode
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

do
	-- Vide's strict mode evaluates every reactive scope twice. A binding that
	-- released its raster from `cleanup()` would, on each of those, drop the
	-- entry's last reference before re-acquiring it — destroying and
	-- re-rasterizing an image for nothing. Handing over explicitly is what makes
	-- this scenario cost one raster instead of several.
	vide.strict = true
	local renderer, cache = newScenario()
	local size = vide.source(24)

	local destroy = vide.root(function()
		return Svg({ source = SEARCH, size = size })
	end)

	equal("strict mode never destroys the live raster", #renderer.destroyed, 0)
	equal("and holds exactly one reference", stats(cache).referenceCount, 1)
	equal("having rasterized once", #renderer.images, 1)

	size(48)
	equal("after a change it still holds one reference", stats(cache).referenceCount, 1)
	equal("and one entry", stats(cache).entryCount, 1)
	equal("and rasterized the new size once", #renderer.images, 2)

	destroy()
	equal("strict mode leaves nothing referenced", stats(cache).referenceCount, 0)
	equal("and nothing cached", stats(cache).entryCount, 0)
	equal("every image it made was destroyed", #renderer.destroyed, #renderer.images)
	vide.strict = false
end

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

print(`vide: {passed} passed, {failed} failed`)
if failed > 0 then
	for _, failure in failures do
		print(`  FAIL {failure}`)
	end
	error(`{failed} Vide assertion(s) failed`, 0)
end

FILE: tests/transformer/ast.test.ts

/**
 * The AST rewrite, checked by printing.
 *
 * These run the real transformer factory through `ts.transform` and print the
 * result, because printed text is the same thing roblox-ts feeds back into its
 * language service — asserting on node identity would pass while the emitted
 * source said something else entirely.
 *
 * What matters most here is what is *not* touched: a transformer that rewrites
 * any string ending in `.svg` would quietly corrupt unrelated code.
 */

import { mkdirSync, mkdtempSync, rmSync, writeFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { tmpdir } from "node:os";
import { dirname, join } from "node:path";
import { afterEach, beforeEach, describe, expect, it } from "vitest";
import ts from "typescript";

import { DEFAULT_OUT_DIR, generatedModulePath } from "@rbxts/svg-compiler/paths";
import { createSvgTransformer } from "@rbxts/svg-transformer";

let projectDir: string;
let rootDir: string;
let outDir: string;

beforeEach(() => {
	projectDir = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), "rbxts-svg-ast-"));
	rootDir = join(projectDir, "src");
	outDir = join(rootDir, DEFAULT_OUT_DIR);
	mkdirSync(rootDir, { recursive: true });
});

afterEach(() => {
	rmSync(projectDir, { recursive: true, force: true });
});

/** Creates a `.svg` and the generated module the transformer expects beside it. */
function addAsset(relativePath: string): void {
	const sourcePath = join(rootDir, relativePath);
	mkdirSync(dirname(sourcePath), { recursive: true });
	writeFileSync(sourcePath, '<svg viewBox="0 0 1 1"/>', "utf8");

	const modulePath = generatedModulePath(sourcePath, { rootDir, outDir });
	mkdirSync(dirname(modulePath), { recursive: true });
	writeFileSync(modulePath, "export default 0;\n", "utf8");
}

interface TransformOutcome {
	readonly text: string;
	readonly diagnostics: readonly string[];
}

/** Transforms one file's source and returns the printed result. */
function transform(fileName: string, source: string): TransformOutcome {
	const sourceFile = ts.createSourceFile(
		join(rootDir, fileName),
		source,
		ts.ScriptTarget.ESNext,
		/* setParentNodes */ true,
		fileName.endsWith(".tsx") ? ts.ScriptKind.TSX : ts.ScriptKind.TS,
	);

	const result = ts.transform(sourceFile, [
		createSvgTransformer({ tsApi: ts, config: { rootDir, outDir } }),
	]);
	const printed = ts.createPrinter().printFile(result.transformed[0]!);
	const diagnostics = (result.diagnostics ?? []).map((diagnostic) =>
		ts.flattenDiagnosticMessageText(diagnostic.messageText, "\n"),
	);
	result.dispose();
	return { text: printed, diagnostics };
}

describe("import rewriting", () => {
	it("rewrites a default import of a sibling .svg", () => {
		addAsset("icon.svg");
		const { text, diagnostics } = transform("main.ts", `import Icon from "./icon.svg";\n`);
		expect(diagnostics).toEqual([]);
		expect(text).toContain(`import Icon from "./svg-cache/icon.svg"`);
	});

	it("rewrites from a nested importer without hardcoding depth", () => {
		addAsset("assets/icons/search.svg");
		const { text, diagnostics } = transform(
			"screens/settings/Settings.tsx",
			`import Search from "../../assets/icons/search.svg";\n`,
		);
		expect(diagnostics).toEqual([]);
		expect(text).toContain(`"../../svg-cache/assets/icons/search.svg"`);
	});

	it("rewrites a re-export", () => {
		addAsset("icon.svg");
		const { text, diagnostics } = transform(
			"index.ts",
			`export { default as Icon } from "./icon.svg";\n`,
		);
		expect(diagnostics).toEqual([]);
		expect(text).toContain(`export { default as Icon } from "./svg-cache/icon.svg"`);
	});

	it("rewrites a bare default re-export", () => {
		addAsset("icon.svg");
		const { text } = transform("index.ts", `export { default } from "./icon.svg";\n`);
		expect(text).toContain(`export { default } from "./svg-cache/icon.svg"`);
	});

	it("preserves a type-only import's modifier", () => {
		addAsset("icon.svg");
		const { text } = transform("main.ts", `import type Icon from "./icon.svg";\n`);
		expect(text).toContain(`import type Icon from "./svg-cache/icon.svg"`);
	});

	it("preserves a namespace import clause", () => {
		addAsset("icon.svg");
		const { text } = transform("main.ts", `import * as Icon from "./icon.svg";\n`);
		expect(text).toContain(`import * as Icon from "./svg-cache/icon.svg"`);
	});

	it("rewrites a side-effect-only import", () => {
		addAsset("icon.svg");
		const { text } = transform("main.ts", `import "./icon.svg";\n`);
		expect(text).toContain(`import "./svg-cache/icon.svg"`);
	});
});

describe("what it leaves alone", () => {
	it("does not touch ordinary imports", () => {
		const { text, diagnostics } = transform(
			"main.ts",
			`import { something } from "./normal-module";\n`,
		);
		expect(diagnostics).toEqual([]);
		expect(text).toContain(`from "./normal-module"`);
	});

	it("does not touch a string that merely ends in .svg", () => {
		const { text, diagnostics } = transform(
			"main.ts",
			`const value = "./icon.svg";\nconst other = { path: "../a/b.svg" };\n`,
		);
		expect(diagnostics).toEqual([]);
		expect(text).toContain(`"./icon.svg"`);
		expect(text).toContain(`"../a/b.svg"`);
		expect(text).not.toContain("svg-cache");
	});

	it("does not touch imports inside the generated directory", () => {
		addAsset("icon.svg");
		const outcome = transform(
			join(DEFAULT_OUT_DIR, "icon.svg.ts"),
			`import { unstable_internal } from "@rbxts/svg";\nimport X from "../icon.svg";\n`,
		);
		expect(outcome.diagnostics).toEqual([]);
		expect(outcome.text).toContain(`"../icon.svg"`);
		expect(outcome.text).not.toContain("svg-cache");
	});

	it("does not rewrite an already-generated specifier a second time", () => {
		addAsset("icons/search.svg");
		const { text, diagnostics } = transform(
			"main.ts",
			`import Search from "./svg-cache/icons/search.svg";\n`,
		);
		expect(diagnostics).toEqual([]);
		expect(text).toContain(`"./svg-cache/icons/search.svg"`);
		expect(text).not.toContain("svg-cache/svg-cache");
	});
});

describe("diagnostics", () => {
	it("reports a missing .svg and leaves the specifier in place", () => {
		const { text, diagnostics } = transform("main.ts", `import Icon from "./missing.svg";\n`);
		expect(diagnostics).toHaveLength(1);
		expect(diagnostics[0]).toContain("cannot resolve SVG import");
		expect(text).toContain(`"./missing.svg"`);
	});

	it("reports a missing generated module", () => {
		const sourcePath = join(rootDir, "icon.svg");
		writeFileSync(sourcePath, '<svg viewBox="0 0 1 1"/>', "utf8");
		const { diagnostics } = transform("main.ts", `import Icon from "./icon.svg";\n`);
		expect(diagnostics).toHaveLength(1);
		expect(diagnostics[0]).toContain("generated asset module is missing");
	});

	it("reports a non-relative .svg specifier", () => {
		const { diagnostics } = transform("main.ts", `import Icon from "@/icons/search.svg";\n`);
		expect(diagnostics).toHaveLength(1);
		expect(diagnostics[0]).toContain("only relative .svg imports are supported");
	});

	it("reports a dynamic import of a .svg", () => {
		addAsset("icon.svg");
		const { diagnostics } = transform(
			"main.ts",
			`export async function load() { return import("./icon.svg"); }\n`,
		);
		expect(diagnostics).toHaveLength(1);
		expect(diagnostics[0]).toContain("only static imports of .svg files are supported");
	});

	it("reports import = require() of a .svg", () => {
		addAsset("icon.svg");
		const { diagnostics } = transform("main.ts", `import Icon = require("./icon.svg");\n`);
		expect(diagnostics).toHaveLength(1);
		expect(diagnostics[0]).toContain("only static imports of .svg files are supported");
	});

	it("anchors the diagnostic on the specifier, not the whole statement", () => {
		const sourceFile = ts.createSourceFile(
			join(rootDir, "main.ts"),
			`import Icon from "./missing.svg";\n`,
			ts.ScriptTarget.ESNext,
			true,
		);
		const result = ts.transform(sourceFile, [
			createSvgTransformer({ tsApi: ts, config: { rootDir, outDir } }),
		]);
		const diagnostic = result.diagnostics?.[0];
		result.dispose();

		expect(diagnostic).toBeDefined();
		expect(sourceFile.text.slice(diagnostic!.start, diagnostic!.start + diagnostic!.length)).toBe(
			`"./missing.svg"`,
		);
	});

	it("leaves a dynamic import of a non-SVG module alone", () => {
		const { diagnostics } = transform(
			"main.ts",
			`export async function load() { return import("./other"); }\n`,
		);
		expect(diagnostics).toEqual([]);
	});
});

FILE: tests/transformer/paths.test.ts
================================================
/**
 * The specifier mapping, on its own.
 *
 * Everything here is a pure function, so these tests are about the properties
 * the rest of the pipeline relies on: that the emitted specifier is POSIX and
 * relative on every host, that the acceptance rules match the generator's, and
 * that the transformer never rewrites something that is not an SVG import.
 *
 * The Windows cases run on POSIX machines and vice versa: `node:path` exports
 * `win32` and `posix` implementations, and the mapping takes whichever it is
 * handed. Cross-platform behaviour is not something to find out about from a CI
 * runner that happens to be Linux.
 */

import { join, resolve } from "node:path";
import { describe, expect, it } from "vitest";

import {
	DEFAULT_OUT_DIR,
	SvgOutsideRootError,
	generatedModulePath,
	generatedModuleSpecifier,
	isInside,
	isRelativeSpecifier,
	isSvgSpecifier,
	posixPaths,
	resolveOutDir,
	toModuleSpecifier,
	windowsPaths,
} from "@rbxts/svg-compiler/paths";
import { mapSpecifier, shouldTransformFile } from "@rbxts/svg-transformer";
import type { FileSystemHost } from "@rbxts/svg-transformer";

const ROOT = resolve("/project/src");
const OUT = join(ROOT, DEFAULT_OUT_DIR);
const CONFIG = { rootDir: ROOT, outDir: OUT };

/** A filesystem where a fixed set of paths exists and nothing else does. */
function fakeHost(...existing: string[]): FileSystemHost {
	const set = new Set(existing.map((path) => resolve(path)));
	return { fileExists: (path) => set.has(resolve(path)) };
}

/** The two files a successful mapping needs to find. */
function bothExist(source: string): FileSystemHost {
	return fakeHost(source, generatedModulePath(source, CONFIG));
}

describe("generatedModulePath", () => {
	it("mirrors the source tree under the generated directory", () => {
		expect(generatedModulePath(join(ROOT, "icons/search.svg"), CONFIG)).toBe(
			join(OUT, "icons/search.svg.ts"),
		);
	});

	it("is stable regardless of how deep the source sits", () => {
		expect(generatedModulePath(join(ROOT, "a/b/c/d/icon.svg"), CONFIG)).toBe(
			join(OUT, "a/b/c/d/icon.svg.ts"),
		);
	});

	it("honours a custom generated directory outside the source root", () => {
		const custom = { rootDir: ROOT, outDir: resolve("/project/generated") };
		expect(generatedModulePath(join(ROOT, "icons/search.svg"), custom)).toBe(
			resolve("/project/generated/icons/search.svg.ts"),
		);
	});

	it("refuses a source outside the root, exactly as the generator does", () => {
		expect(() => generatedModulePath(resolve("/elsewhere/icon.svg"), CONFIG)).toThrow(
			SvgOutsideRootError,
		);
	});

	it("defaults the generated directory to <rootDir>/svg-cache", () => {
		expect(resolveOutDir({ rootDir: ROOT })).toBe(OUT);
	});
});

describe("generatedModuleSpecifier", () => {
	const cases: ReadonlyArray<readonly [string, string, string, string]> = [
		["same directory", "", "icon.svg", "./svg-cache/icon.svg"],
		["a sibling directory", "", "icons/search.svg", "./svg-cache/icons/search.svg"],
		["one level down", "ui", "icons/search.svg", "../svg-cache/icons/search.svg"],
		[
			"a deeply nested importer",
			"screens/settings/panels",
			"assets/icons/search.svg",
			"../../../svg-cache/assets/icons/search.svg",
		],
		[
			"an importer already inside the mirrored tree",
			"assets/icons",
			"assets/icons/search.svg",
			"../../svg-cache/assets/icons/search.svg",
		],
	];

	for (const [name, importerDir, source, expected] of cases) {
		it(`maps ${name}`, () => {
			expect(
				generatedModuleSpecifier(join(ROOT, importerDir), join(ROOT, source), CONFIG),
			).toBe(expected);
		});
	}

	it("drops the generated .ts suffix", () => {
		// Node10 resolution — which roblox-ts pins — finds `search.svg.ts` from
		// `./…/search.svg` by adding the extension itself.
		expect(generatedModuleSpecifier(ROOT, join(ROOT, "a.svg"), CONFIG)).not.toContain(".ts");
	});

	it("produces the same POSIX specifier from Windows paths", () => {
		const config = { rootDir: "C:\\project\\src", outDir: "C:\\project\\src\\svg-cache" };
		expect(
			generatedModuleSpecifier(
				"C:\\project\\src\\screens\\settings",
				"C:\\project\\src\\assets\\icons\\search.svg",
				config,
				windowsPaths,
			),
		).toBe("../../svg-cache/assets/icons/search.svg");
	});

	it("produces the same POSIX specifier from POSIX paths", () => {
		const config = { rootDir: "/project/src", outDir: "/project/src/svg-cache" };
		expect(
			generatedModuleSpecifier(
				"/project/src/screens/settings",
				"/project/src/assets/icons/search.svg",
				config,
				posixPaths,
			),
		).toBe("../../svg-cache/assets/icons/search.svg");
	});

	it("rejects a Windows source on another drive", () => {
		expect(() =>
			generatedModulePath(
				"D:\\elsewhere\\icon.svg",
				{ rootDir: "C:\\project\\src" },
				windowsPaths,
			),
		).toThrow(SvgOutsideRootError);
	});
});

describe("toModuleSpecifier", () => {
	it("normalizes Windows separators", () => {
		expect(toModuleSpecifier("..\\svg-cache\\icons\\search.svg")).toBe(
			"../svg-cache/icons/search.svg",
		);
	});

	it("adds ./ so a sibling is not read as a package name", () => {
		expect(toModuleSpecifier("svg-cache/foo.svg")).toBe("./svg-cache/foo.svg");
	});

	it("leaves an already-relative specifier alone", () => {
		expect(toModuleSpecifier("../a/b.svg")).toBe("../a/b.svg");
	});
});

describe("predicates", () => {
	it("recognizes .svg specifiers case-insensitively", () => {
		expect(isSvgSpecifier("./a.svg")).toBe(true);
		expect(isSvgSpecifier("./a.SVG")).toBe(true);
		expect(isSvgSpecifier("./a.svgz")).toBe(false);
		expect(isSvgSpecifier("@rbxts/svg")).toBe(false);
	});

	it("treats only ./ and ../ as relative", () => {
		expect(isRelativeSpecifier("./a.svg")).toBe(true);
		expect(isRelativeSpecifier("../a.svg")).toBe(true);
		expect(isRelativeSpecifier("@/a.svg")).toBe(false);
		expect(isRelativeSpecifier("assets/a.svg")).toBe(false);
	});

	it("does not mistake a sibling directory for a nested one", () => {
		expect(isInside(resolve("/a/bcd"), resolve("/a/bc"))).toBe(false);
		expect(isInside(resolve("/a/bc/d"), resolve("/a/bc"))).toBe(true);
	});
});

describe("mapSpecifier", () => {
	const importer = join(ROOT, "ui/Toolbar.tsx");
	const source = join(ROOT, "icons/search.svg");

	it("rewrites a relative .svg import", () => {
		const result = mapSpecifier(importer, "../icons/search.svg", CONFIG, bothExist(source));
		expect(result).toEqual({
			kind: "rewrite",
			specifier: "../svg-cache/icons/search.svg",
			sourcePath: source,
			modulePath: join(OUT, "icons/search.svg.ts"),
		});
	});

	it("leaves non-SVG specifiers alone without touching the filesystem", () => {
		const explode: FileSystemHost = {
			fileExists: () => {
				throw new Error("should not be consulted");
			},
		};
		expect(mapSpecifier(importer, "./normal-module", CONFIG, explode)).toEqual({ kind: "skip" });
		expect(mapSpecifier(importer, "@rbxts/svg", CONFIG, explode)).toEqual({ kind: "skip" });
	});

	it("leaves an explicit generated-module specifier alone", () => {
		// Still valid to write by hand, and rewriting it would look for a `.svg`
		// source inside the cache that never existed.
		const result = mapSpecifier(importer, "../svg-cache/icons/search.svg", CONFIG, bothExist(source));
		expect(result).toEqual({ kind: "skip" });
	});

	it("reports a non-relative specifier rather than guessing an alias", () => {
		const result = mapSpecifier(importer, "@/icons/search.svg", CONFIG, bothExist(source));
		expect(result.kind).toBe("error");
		expect(result.kind === "error" && result.message).toContain("only relative .svg imports");
	});

	it("reports a source that escapes the root", () => {
		const result = mapSpecifier(importer, "../../../outside.svg", CONFIG, fakeHost());
		expect(result.kind).toBe("error");
		expect(result.kind === "error" && result.message).toContain("outside the source root");
	});

	it("reports a missing .svg, naming the specifier and the importer", () => {
		const result = mapSpecifier(importer, "../icons/nope.svg", CONFIG, fakeHost());
		expect(result.kind).toBe("error");
		if (result.kind !== "error") return;
		expect(result.message).toContain("cannot resolve SVG import");
		expect(result.message).toContain("../icons/nope.svg");
		expect(result.message).toContain("Toolbar.tsx");
	});

	it("reports a missing generated module, naming the build command", () => {
		const result = mapSpecifier(importer, "../icons/search.svg", CONFIG, fakeHost(source));
		expect(result.kind).toBe("error");
		if (result.kind !== "error") return;
		expect(result.message).toContain("generated asset module is missing");
		expect(result.message).toContain("search.svg.ts");
		expect(result.message).toContain("rbxts-svg build");
	});

	it("follows a custom generated directory", () => {
		const custom = { rootDir: ROOT, outDir: resolve("/project/src/generated") };
		const host = fakeHost(source, generatedModulePath(source, custom));
		const result = mapSpecifier(importer, "../icons/search.svg", custom, host);
		expect(result.kind === "rewrite" && result.specifier).toBe(
			"../generated/icons/search.svg",
		);
	});
});

describe("shouldTransformFile", () => {
	it("skips generated modules so they are never remapped again", () => {
		expect(shouldTransformFile(join(OUT, "icons/search.svg.ts"), CONFIG)).toBe(false);
	});

	it("transforms ordinary source files", () => {
		expect(shouldTransformFile(join(ROOT, "ui/Toolbar.tsx"), CONFIG)).toBe(true);
	});
});
